x: Here Penny was leading Les Cohen by 39 secs., with Allum a further 20 secs. behind in third place. Williams, Taylor, Ring, Shields and Flower followed. Then came a batch of runners, led by our Captain, H.E.F.
Soon after this, Bert forged ahead to pass Carter, Flower came up from 10th position to 7th to displace Allum, and Shields dropped back a couple of places.

Shields did well to finish third, and among the others, Ted Stimpson was generally thought to have done well. It was pleasing to see several comparative newcomers showing fair form, which should in due course find them places in our teams.

Ten of our points were amassed in the one and two mile events through the events of Cohen, Carter, Shields and Taylor. Our remaining points came from Lee (440 yards), and Quackenbos and Grassau (High Jump).

George Checkley, improving fast, deserved his handicap win and Jack Coton made use of a generous mark for second place. Third in the handicap was Ted Smith, who just stopped “Pot-hunter” Shields, who filled the fourth place.

Eight miles was reached by Clayton in 70.36, closely followed by McGreechan, Wright and Checkley; 350 yards behind came Bidgood, Bellchambers, Shields and Rutland, and a further 200 yards Wakeley and Readman, closely followed by Sapcote, Sutton and Robins.
Shields (4.40).
George Beecham won the 2 miles walk handicap with our old friend Harry Shields battling away to gain 2nd place from Bill True, the handicapper!

Harry closed in as fourth man, 'pot-hunter' Shields the veteran award winner; Bernard made a good recovery after a bad patch on Dale Hill and he just pipped Jack Keown by two seconds, Jack walked very well for a first-timer and was heard to say that it was easier than an Open 7.

"A Southern Counties 6-Stage Relay was held from Belgrave Hall on April 4th over a four and three-quarter miles lap. Belgrave were winners with Marchant, Patience, Shields, Penny, Cohen and Carter.
The Captain that day was Bert Footer and the rest of the team were Allum, Carter, Flower, Ginty, Parker, Patience; Shaw, Ring, Rice, Shields and Taylor.

On April 29th 1944 Etienne (immediately becoming known as Steve) was elected a member of Belgrave Harriers and he found himself running alongside such notables as Carter, Cohen, Shields and Doubleday.
